To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NGS data analysis of cancer tissue samples from patients who responded to Aurora Kinase A inhibition revealed high connectivity within the Wnt/b-catenin pathway, while patients who did not respond showed high connectivity centered around the TP53/Rb1 axis.
the responding patient population showed a high connectivity within MYCR related genes, while the non-responders showed a high connectivity centered on TP53/RB axis.
the molecular biological pathways associated with MYC and the TP53/RN1 axis are differentially associated with the response to the Aurora kinase inhibitor MLN8237.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular predictors of clinical response to targeted therapies in patients with solid tumors, and with the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of response and resistance.
identifying molecular markers of clinical response and the relationships between molecular markers of response and the molecular biology of the cancer.
the application of “systems biology” to the study of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“the molecular pathways involved in the response of the patients to MLN8237 treatment can be identified by the analysis of NGS sequencing data.”
the NGS mapping of genomic alterations in patients receiving targeted therapy can be used to predict response and to help identify the molecular pathways responsible.

the NGS data analysis in this study suggests that the molecular pathways that were identified as important in this small group of patients with advanced cancer may be important for future clinical trials of this drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the responder group was characterized by high connectivity within MYCR related genes including regulators in Wnt/beta- catenin pathway and the non-responder group was characterized by a high connectivity centered on TP53/RB pathway.
NGS can be a useful tool to help predict response to therapy in patients with advanced cancer.
the NGS analysis of the Aurora kinase inhibitor MLN8237 in patients with advanced solid malignancy revealed a relationship of molecular signal to response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of NGS in cancer research and clinical practice is a powerful tool to identify genomic and proteomic alterations that can be used to predict the clinical response to targeted therapies.
NGS can be a useful tool for identifying genomic alterations in tumors that may be associated with response or lack of response to therapy.
NGS analysis of tumor tissue from patients treated with Aurora Kinase inhibitors can provide insight into the mechanisms of response and nonresponse to therapy.
